DECISIONS:
Q1: B
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: This issue was re-opened because the one-PR attempt (#6151, the "everything at once" scope) grew to 58 conflicting files and fell 77 commits behind `main`, and pipeline issues have a ≤60-minute implement budget. So the scope should be the shared bash helper and its Python twin, plus migration steps 1–4 and 6. Those are the call sites behind the 2026-10-01 incident: the review gates, the validate authorize step, the resolve calls and the sweep that re-dispatches duplicates. Steps 5 (remove the inline retry copies), 7 (the poller's `|| echo "main"` / `|| echo '[]'` fallbacks), 8 (the Python readers) and "re-run after the reset instead of escalating" become separate follow-up issues that link back here. One note for the implementer: `gh_retry` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` (around lines 525–564) already drops a failed attempt's stdout, which fixed #5495, so don't redo that. `gh_retry_to_file` still leaves the last failed attempt's body in the output file, so the new helper's write-only-on-success rule should cover it.
Q2: The issue lists "unsafe retries of creates" as a defect of the existing helpers in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`. Under B that defect stays live for the roughly 68 callers this issue doesn't migrate. The repo already treats non-idempotent creates as single-shot: see the comments at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 6598 and 6781 and `scripts/security_audit.sh` line 2199. A follows that rule and still keeps label adds and dedupe-guarded dispatches retryable through `--idempotent`. C is too broad: PUT, PATCH and DELETE are idempotent by HTTP semantics, and most label and edit calls depend on retrying them. The POST check should also cover gh's own create subcommands (`gh issue create`, `gh pr create`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`), because each one sends a REST POST create.
